free_tier.stated: EUR 3.99/month for VPS-2 in the Netherlands: Intel Xeon Platinum 8173M, 2 vCore, 4 GB DDR4, 50 GB NVMe, 'Unlimited Traffic, fair usage', 2 Gbit/s port. That is the cheapest plan on the vendor page read; the others are VPS-6 at EUR 26.99/month (shown from EUR 29.99, 10 vCore, 32 GB, 280 GB, 10 Gbit/s) and VPS-9 at EUR 80.99/month (from EUR 89.99, 16 vCore, 128 GB, 500 GB, 10 Gbit/s). The tracker's cheapest row is a cheaper product the vendor pages do not list: EUR 1.99/month for 1 Intel core, 2,048 MB RAM, 30 GB NVMe, 50,000 GB/month on a 1 Gbps port, slugged VPS_1_Standard_VPS.

egress.terms: 'Unlimited Traffic, fair usage' on VPS-2 at a 2 Gbit/s port; no number, no overage price and no throttle threshold are stated on the page read

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: order links are form posts to /en/cart?add=vps-std-2&cycle=monthly; no API, panel name or image list appears on the page read
chaining: EUR 3.99 for 2 vCores, 4 GB and 50 GB of NVMe in the Netherlands with no metered transfer is the best ratio of RAM to price after Advin, and 'unlimited, fair usage' suits a crawler front end that cannot predict its monthly bytes the unmeasured fair-use clause is the risk, since the throttle point is unpublished
limits_note: 'Unlimited Traffic, fair usage' with no number is not an allowance, so no volume quota is stated on this plan; the fair-use clause leaves the throttle point unknown rather than absent, and the 2 Gbit/s port is the only published ceiling. The tracker's EUR 1.99 row is the one row that carries a number, 50,000 GB/month, and that figure is the port converted rather than a quota.
